objective: Finish four already-installed M2.5 × 3.75 mm HELICOIL inserts in a portable representative ODRI actuator shell base. Physically grasp and align a straight tang break-off mandrel with each recessed insert, strike it using a separately manipulated hammer so the modeled tang fractures at its notch, then recover all four free tangs into the tray. The shell may be grasped and reoriented, including tipping over the tray, but may never be teleported or secretly attached. Full success requires four credited contact-driven fractures, intact inserts and case, four contained fragments, released and supported case/tools/fragments, valid RGB-D observations, and a stable two-second terminal state.
instruction: Break all four insert tangs using the mandrel and hammer. Keep the inserts and portable shell intact, recover every fragment into the tray, and finish with the shell, tools, and fragments released, supported, and at rest.
industrial_mapping: The pinned Open Dynamic Robot Initiative actuator-module-v1 shell-preparation procedure specifies four M2.5 × 3.75 mm HELICOIL inserts in a standalone printed shell base, removal of their tangs with a tang break-off tool, and verification that tangs do not remain inside the part; it later turns the shell assembly around and reports a complete shell-assembly mass of 61 g (source s-df759bd2377bbb57, pinned commit 66af1522b4fba0ec4a1d7790e66f5e4652208d30). The Böllhoff HELICOIL Plus catalog states that a through-hole insert tang is broken at its notch, depicts hammer actuation of a straight mandrel, and lists straight mandrel 0158 040 1000 for M2.5 (source s-6195df1bebbb33ef, pages 17 and 55). The simulation is an independently authored representative rigid test article, not exact product CAD or a calibrated reconstruction of the historical unitless STL.
damage_rules: Lifecycle and sampling: retain exactly one PRE_PHYSICS_STEP and one POST_PHYSICS_STEP callback handle for the task context. Reset precedes integration and clears state exactly once. Native interval n is (t_(n-1),t_n]; PRE(n) records fresh poses, twists, collision transforms, and joint states, and POST(n) consumes only contacts and transitions from that interval. Production samples 300 s after POST(72000) and times out after POST(86400); refinement uses POST(144000) and POST(172800). Repeated score or success reads cannot advance state. Deregister old handles on reset. Clear step tags, episodes, transitions, impulses, work, penetration, loss, hard failure H, bonuses, camera counters, and hold timers.

Callback timing: for every actual unique POST interval retain the original float32 callback dt_n. Production error is max_n|dt_n-1/240| and refinement error is max_n|dt_n-1/480|. The appropriate maximum must be ≤1e-9 s. Never round dt_n or substitute configuration values. Missing, duplicate, stale, future, untagged, non-finite, callback-exception, wrong-count, or out-of-tolerance intervals invalidate measurement availability and set H; exceptions never become zero-valued observations.

Initial diagnostics: apply zero robot actions for exactly 1.0 s through POST(240) or POST(480). Speed maxima use the last 0.25 s: production POST(181..240), refinement POST(361..480). Evaluate all initial counts, score, relative insert motion, joint integrity, penetration, and open episodes immediately after the sampling POST and before control action 1. Initial penetration is the maximum over every diagnostic POST. Any J_shell_q or J_seat_i transition during this window fails its explicit initial count and sets H. Empty contact/event sets cannot establish availability if callback or native-stream acquisition failed.

Body sets: B_case comprises every portable shell-base/cover rigid body; B_fixture comprises only the world-stationary station jig; B_insert={retained_coil_i}; B_tang={tang_i}; B_tool comprises mandrel plus hammer head/handle; B_fragment is the released subset of B_tang; B_robot is every robot collision link; B_tray is tray floor/walls. J_shell_q connects actual case parts to the designated portable case root, never to world. J_seat_i connects insert i to its seat in B_case. The stationary jig has separately named joints J_jig_q. Native body and joint identities are frozen at reset and must remain addressable.

Contact quantities: C_n is the complete fresh native contact-point set from interval n. A native force f_c,n in N becomes impulse J_c,n=f_c,n*dt_n exactly once; a native impulse in N*s is used directly. Verify the selected field, direction, units, sign, finite values, identity mapping, and freshness using native material contact. Point velocity is v_b(p)=v_b,COM+omega_b×(p-x_b,COM), using PRE(n). No nominal force schedule or empty contact stream proves a force path.

Impact episodes open on first fresh compressive hammer_head↔mandrel contact. They include consecutive samples and gaps shorter than 1/240 s and close after accumulated contact-free time reaches 1/240 s: one absent production sample or two absent refinement samples. Gap samples add no impulse. A solver tick alone cannot create an episode. Each of all four inserts must have at least one closed strike that caused its credited transition for completed-insert-strike-count-minimum.

A credited strike for tang i requires at least one identical native step n containing compressive hammer_head↔mandrel and mandrel↔tang_i contacts. Contacts appearing only in different steps do not qualify. No hammer_head↔tang/insert/case, robot_link↔tang/insert, or tray-as-striking-tool contact is allowed in a credited episode.

Each tang_i is an independent rigid body connected only to retained_coil_i by native breakable fixed joint J_tang_i. A physical fracture is strictly an intact-at-PRE(n) to broken-at-POST(n) transition. Joint transitions occur physically before eligibility is evaluated and are never suppressed. Non-target J_tang transition, J_seat/J_shell/J_jig break, body deletion, scripted transition, or unavailable joint state sets H while retaining the physical outcome.

Shared case-frame geometry: at reset define case frame C from the actual portable case root transform T_WC, and define each seat baseline T_CI_i,0=T_WC,0^-1 T_WI_i,0. The shared insert axis a_C,i, seat origin o_C,i, mandrel targets, radial calculations, collision sets, and scorer locations all come from one frozen geometry definition. At PRE/POST sample T_CI_i=T_WC^-1 T_WI_i. Axial displacement is |(x_CI_i-x_CI_i,0)·a_C,i|. Angular displacement is acos(clamp((trace(R_CI_i,0^T R_CI_i)-1)/2,-1,1)). Initial axial motion >0.0001 m fails initialization; later axial motion >0.00025 m, rotation >3 degrees, J_seat breakage, coil fracture, or withdrawal beyond the seat interval sets H. Rigid whole-case motion alone is not insert damage.

For strike i, transform a_C,i into world using the PRE case rotation. Orient hammer impulse as applied to the mandrel. J_ax,i=Σmax(0,J_c,n·a_W,i). For every mandrel contact with hammer head, target tang, insert, or boss, j_perp=J_c,n-(J_c,n·a_W,i)a_W,i and J_offaxis,i=Σ||j_perp||; lateral impulses cannot cancel. At closure, J_ax>0.035 N*s or J_offaxis>0.008 N*s sets H regardless of fracture. More than three closed strikes for one insert, striking after release, direct forbidden hammer contact, fracture by robot link, carrying/striking with the stationary fixture, or using the tray as a striking tool sets H. Legitimate grasping, carrying, and tipping of the portable intact case is permitted.

Axis angle is acos(clamp(u_m·a_W,i,-1,1)) at PRE contact onset. Radial offset is ||(I-a_W,i a_W,i^T)(p_tip-p_axis,i)|| using the shared seat geometry. Credit requires the simultaneous force path, target J_tang transition, J_ax∈[0.012,0.035] N*s, J_offaxis≤0.008 N*s, angle≤5 degrees, offset≤0.00035 m, and no H. Each tang earns credit once.

Shell damage is W_shell=Σmax(0,J_onV·(v_A(p)-v_V(p))) over unordered contacts where vulnerable V is a case/boss body contacted by tool, robot, tang, or coil, or a retained coil contacted by a free tang. Use PRE point velocities. Exclude intended hammer_head↔mandrel, mandrel↔target_tang, tang↔tray, case↔tray/table during non-impact support/reorientation, and tool↔support contacts. W_shell resets only at episode reset and is monotonic. W_shell>0.02 J, any J_shell/J_seat break, or direct hammer_head↔case sets H. This is an incident-energy proxy, not calibrated cracking.

Signed penetration uses the exact PhysX collision primitives or frozen finite convex unions. Deterministic double-precision GJK gives positive separation when disjoint; touching within 1e-9 m gives s=0; intersection uses EPA and s=-d_EPA. For unions, geometry separation is the minimum constituent separation and penetration P=max(0,-s). Exclude only intact notch mating faces, authored coil-seat mating faces, and declared structural case-part mating faces. Track maximum P initially and after every fracture for case, inserts, bosses, mandrel, hammer, tray, robot, jig, and fragments. P>0.0002 m or mandrel intrusion beyond the target notch plane sets H. Unsupported collision meshes block construction.

A safe grasp of body q requires fresh inward-normal contacts from both named fingers of one gripper, no table/tray/catch support, lowest collision point ≥0.002 m above its last support plane, and palm-relative pose drift ≤0.001 m and ≤2 degrees for 0.25 s. It becomes unheld after 0.10 s without gripper contact and with native support. Apply this predicate independently to mandrel, hammer, and portable case. Pre-held, welded, pose-driven, or hidden-attached bodies earn nothing and set H where used as success evidence.

Alignment holds when a post-reset safe mandrel grasp exists and, for 0.25 s of unique POST times, radial offset≤0.00035 m, angle≤5 degrees, fresh mandrel_tip↔unbroken_tang contact exists, and no forbidden penetration or fracture occurs. Alignment persists after legitimate withdrawal, subject to H.

Fragment j is contained iff every point of its complete transformed collision geometry G_j lies in the closed tray interior prism, fresh tray support has upward normal, linear speed≤0.01 m/s, and angular speed≤0.5 rad/s. Credit is current-state and revoked immediately when any condition fails.

Loss is irreversible when any point of complete fragment geometry crosses outside the closed workcell bound, all geometry crosses the floor-loss plane, state becomes non-finite, or the native body is deleted/unaddressable. A fragment merely outside the tray remains unfinished. At timeout, inaccessibility requires all G_j to lie in a visible closed free-space component whose every continuous collision-free opening to robot-accessible workspace is narrower than the fragment’s smallest oriented collision extent, computed deterministically using Minkowski-expanded frozen collision geometry. Planner failure, elapsed time, labels, or absence from the tray do not establish inaccessibility. Loss or proven inaccessibility sets H.

Terminal rest requires four contained fragments and every physical task body—portable case, mandrel, hammer, and fragments—unheld, natively supported, with linear speed≤0.01 m/s and angular speed≤0.5 rad/s; the stationary fixture must remain ≤0.002 m/s; no strike may be open. The case and tools need not return to their initial poses. The conditions must hold continuously for 2.0 s at distinct POST times; active carrying never counts.

Camera mask M is the union of pixels in the projected convex hull of all eight declared task-AABB corners and pixels bearing case, insert/tang, tool, tray, or fragment geometry IDs. Starting at a valid 20 Hz observation t0, require 41 newly consumed frames at t0+m/20 s for m=0..40. Timestamps must strictly increase and lie in [target,target+0.05 s]. Every AABB corner must have positive camera depth and project inside image bounds; RGB on M must be finite; count(finite depth>0 on M)/|M|≥0.99. Never shrink/fill M, replace missing depth, reuse stale frames, or count duplicates. Any invalid frame resets the hold.

Unsafe self-contact set S_self includes all cross-arm collision-link pairs and same-arm pairs separated by at least two joints, excluding intended finger↔held-body contact. Any fresh normal impulse >0.02 N*s sets H. Non-finite data, stale camera reuse, callback duplication, or tool/fragment escape also sets H.

Task bodies may move only through robot actuation/contact, native joints, native rigid-body contact, and gravity. Pose/velocity writes, teleportation, deletion, hidden grasp welds, collision suppression, magnetic/airflow cleanup forces, unsupported through-holes, or flags derived from waypoint, timer, desired action, object ID, or scripted grasp state used as physical success evidence set H. Bad physical outcomes remain possible and then fail scoring. Safe alternative strategies, including sequential manipulation and tipping the portable case over the tray, remain eligible.
assets: Independently authored elongated portable rigid shell-base/cover assembly with representative bosses, recesses, access openings, declared case frame, shared insert geometry, and a reasonable empty-shell mass bounded below the sourced 61 g complete assembly; not exact CAD
Separate world-stationary station jig with named integrity joints J_jig_q
Four retained rigid HELICOIL proxies, four distinct tang bodies, native breakable J_tang_i joints, case-relative J_seat_i joints, and structural J_shell_q joints
Representative straight M2.5 tang break-off mandrel with shaft clearance derived from the shared geometry
Representative small hammer with unscaled rigid Xform root and separately scaled collision/render children; native fixed head-handle joint
Rigid containment tray with floor and raised walls, table, and bounded catch surface
YAM dual-arm robot with physical grippers and declared self-collision pairs
Fixed, lit 640×480 RGB-D task camera with genuine geometry-ID and depth acquisition
approximations: The ODRI procedure establishes four M2.5 × 3.75 mm inserts, portable shell handling, tang removal, and a 61 g complete shell-assembly bound, but not exact local CAD. Boss spacing, recess depth, cavity geometry, access clearance, and empty-base mass are frozen representative assumptions.
The historical unitless shell STL is qualitative shape context only and is not evidence of scale or current geometry.

The 0.012–0.035 N*s axial window, 0.008 N*s off-axis limit, 0.02 J work limit, 0.02 N*s self-contact limit, notch section, wire diameter, masses, friction, restitution, break force/torque, and tool dimensions are uncalibrated prototype assumptions.

The 0.35 mm radial, 5 degree angular, 0.25 mm retention, 3 degree rotation, 0.2 mm penetration, 0.01 m/s rest, 0.5 rad/s rest, and two-second hold limits are frozen scoring assumptions requiring native validation, not manufacturer tolerances.

Fracture is approximated by a native breakable fixed joint at the modeled notch. Invalid impacts may still break or displace bodies and remain represented; fragments are never hidden, deleted, or reattached.

All task geometry is rigid PhysX geometry using primitives or deterministic convex decomposition. No deformable solver, exact helical-wire contact, material-rate model, or calibrated shell-crack model is claimed.
Incident work is a monotonic proxy from fresh native impulse and PRE relative contact-point velocity, not plastic work or fracture energy.
Pinned source inspection establishes only callback API availability. It does not validate contact fields, units, timing, state freshness, reset, fracture, camera, or scoring behavior.
The evaluator control clock is 20 Hz. Physics is independently 240 Hz and refinement 480 Hz; 7200 control steps equal 360 s. Physics substeps never define control time.
Native float32 dt wire values are preserved; the 1e-9 s checks measure representation error against exact reciprocal target rates and do not weaken either frequency.

Failure of component mechanics, camera acquisition, timestep convergence, penetration queries, initial integrity, contact-force paths, or any control rejects the environment and does not authorize relaxed thresholds.
This is a prospective frozen specification, not a claim that the historical scaffold or failed native aggregate implements or passes it.
scoring_spec: Let H be irreversible until actual episode reset. At each unique POST(n), first validate callback availability and dt, then consume native contacts/joints once, update physical transitions and damage, close/classify episodes, update bonuses, and compute score. If H=true, score=0; otherwise score=min(1,G+A+F+R+C+T). G=0.10 after the mandrel and hammer each independently satisfy a post-reset safe grasp; it persists after legitimate release. A=0.10 after valid post-reset alignment holds 0.25 s at an initially unbroken tang; it persists after withdrawal. F=0.10 per distinct credited tang fracture, capped at 0.40. R=0.10 iff all four fracture credits exist, all J_seat_i and J_shell_q remain intact, every insert’s case-relative displacement/rotation remains within 0.25 mm/3 degrees, and shell damage is false; it is ineligible before four credits and revoked immediately on violation. C=0.05 per distinct released tang currently contained, capped at 0.20, and revoked immediately when containment fails. T=0.10 iff four native and credited fractures exist, R is eligible, all four fragments are contained, portable case/tools/fragments are unheld, supported, and at rest, the stationary jig is stable, no strike is open, and 41 consecutive valid 20 Hz RGB-D frames span the same continuous 2.0 s physical hold; T is revoked if any terminal condition breaks. Untouched score is exactly 0. At timeout, evaluate deterministic loss/inaccessibility before scoring. Reset clears all event state, baselines, credits, extrema, accumulators, and camera state. All observables, body/contact sets, force-versus-impulse conversion, PRE/POST ordering, segmentation, accumulation, reset, signed penetration, loss, accessibility, eligibility, and revocation are defined in damage_rules and must replay from raw native records.

required_controls.name: untouched-initial-zero-score
required_controls.reason: No post-reset grasp, alignment, fracture, retention eligibility, containment, or terminal event exists; all initial integrity checks must also be available and pass.

required_controls.name: aligned-subthreshold-tap-at-300s
required_controls.reason: G=0.10 and A=0.10; every closed strike has J_ax<0.012 N*s and J_offaxis≤0.008 N*s, so F=R=C=T=0.

required_controls.name: offaxis-glancing-strike-closed-episode-failure
required_controls.reason: J_offaxis>0.008 N*s at closure sets H while preserving the physical result.

required_controls.name: overimpulse-strike-closed-episode-failure
required_controls.reason: J_ax>0.035 N*s at closure sets H even if the native joint fractures.

required_controls.name: fourth-distinct-strike-failure
required_controls.reason: A fourth closed strike for one insert sets H; uninterrupted solver contact remains one strike.

required_controls.name: direct-hammer-tang-contact-failure
required_controls.reason: Direct hammer contact violates the force path and sets H while native breakage remains possible.

required_controls.name: one-valid-fracture-at-300s
required_controls.reason: G=0.10+A=0.10+F=0.10; the accessible fragment is not contained and R is ineligible.

required_controls.name: four-valid-fractures-three-contained-at-300s
required_controls.reason: G=0.10+A=0.10+F=0.40+R=0.10+C=0.15; the accessible fourth fragment prevents T.

required_controls.name: inaccessible-fragment-at-360s-failure
required_controls.reason: Timeout geometric inaccessibility sets H before final scoring.

required_controls.name: insert-seat-relative-displacement-failure
required_controls.reason: Out-of-tolerance insert motion relative to its moving case, or J_seat breakage, sets H; whole-case carrying alone does not.

required_controls.name: shell-work-joint-or-forbidden-penetration-failure
required_controls.reason: Excess work, any shell joint break, or signed penetration above 0.2 mm sets H.

required_controls.name: fragment-workcell-escape-failure
required_controls.reason: Geometric escape, loss-plane crossing, non-finite state, deletion, or unaddressability sets H.

required_controls.name: complete-stable-terminal-full-score
required_controls.reason: G 0.10+A 0.10+F 0.40+R 0.10+C 0.20+T 0.10 after all bodies are released/supported and the two-second camera-valid hold completes.

required_controls.name: clean-reset-replay-full-score
required_controls.reason: A second real-action trajectory must reproduce full score after callback deregistration and complete reset.

required_controls.name: refinement-480hz-replay-full-score
required_controls.reason: The twice-rate replay must preserve physical-time episode segmentation, outcomes, containment, camera cadence, and score while passing the refinement dt-error check.

required_controls.name: slow-press-outcome-bounded-characterization-at-300s
required_controls.reason: After safe grasps and alignment, park the hammer without hammer↔mandrel contact; press the mandrel axially at 0.0001 m/s for 1.0 s with 8 N saturation, hold 0.25 s, and retract at 0.0001 m/s for 1.0 s. Hammer-path impulses are zero. Require no fracture or H, yielding G+A=0.20; any higher safe score rejects characterization.

required_controls.name: one-hand-characterization-at-300s
required_controls.reason: One arm sequentially grasps the mandrel then hammer, never holds both simultaneously, establishes alignment, and keeps every hammer episode subthreshold. Expected G+A=0.20; fracture, H, or a higher safe score rejects characterization.
